I00045.Description:
RE32601, Saivarahasyam. The text entitled as stotrāṇi, the manuscript bundle is a valuable compilation of devotional hymns and the names dedicated to various deities. It includes Umāmaheśvarāṣṭottara from the Śivarahasya, Lalitāṣṭottaraśatam, Mīnākṣyaṣṭakam, Vighneśvarastotram from the Skāndapurāṇa, Indrākṣīstotram, Āditya-hṛdayam, Mārgasahāyāṣṭakam, Vighneśvarāṣṭottaranāmam, and rituals for Rudrapūjā. All together, these texts reflect a wide spectrum of stotra literature, spanning Śaiva, Śākta, and Sūrya traditions, serving both liturgical and devotional purposes.

The bundle consists of 55 folios, each measuring 210 mm in length and 35 mm in breadth, written in 6–7 lines per folio. The text is preserved in Sanskrit, recorded in both Grantha and Telugu scripts. Although the physical condition of the bundle is damaged and not well-preserved, it remains a significant witness to the transmission of multi-deity stotra traditions and their survival in diverse regional scripts.

I00060.Description:
RE31059 Aṣṭādaśakriyā. This bundle focuses on specific elements of the eighteen ritual processes (kriyās) connected with pratiṣṭhā (consecration). It includes the Pratiṣṭhādhivāsanavidhi, which details the preliminary sanctification rites performed before installation. This is followed by sections on Tattvārchanā and Sparśāhuti, which elaborate on the ritual worship of tattvas. The final section includes partial sections of the Gaurīpratiṣṭhā detailing procedures for installing the goddess Gaurī; however, it appears incomplete.

The manuscript comprises 39 folios, each measuring 41.5 cm × 3.5 cm and containing 7–8 lines of text per folio. This bundle offers focused insight into specific ritual segments within the broader framework of pratiṣṭhā, making it a useful source for understanding the procedural depth of Śaiva consecration practices.
